definitions.explanation: Describes something that shows visible signs of age or wear. Used as a pre-noun modifier (the past-tense form of the verb {古|ふる}びる, functioning adjectivally).

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}びた{本|ほん}を{見|み}つけた。
{古|ふる}びた{建物|たてもの}が{並|なら}ぶ{通|とお}りを{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: I walked along a street lined with weathered buildings.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{家|いえ}には{古|ふる}びた{家具|かぐ}がたくさん{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: My grandfather's house still has a lot of worn old furniture.

notes:
USAGE:
{古|ふる}びた is the past-tense form of the verb {古|ふる}びる (to become old-looking), used as a pre-noun modifier. It describes objects that have taken on an aged appearance through the passage of time.
{古|ふる}びた is neutral — it can suggest charm and character (like antiques) or simply describe something showing wear. Compare with {古|ふる}い, which simply means "old" without emphasizing the visual impression of aging.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古|ふる}びた{建物|たてもの} (a weathered building)
- {古|ふる}びた{写真|しゃしん} (an old-looking photo)
- {古|ふる}びた{街並|まちな}み (an aged townscape)
